meta.title: Phonology: Sounds & Stress
meta.randomizationRule: Randomize question selection/order and answer-option order on every attempt; never reuse an exact attempt signature.
meta.alignment: TKT Module 1 — Describing language: Phonology — IPA symbols, phonemes, word stress and sentence stress
meta.scopeNote: Intonation, linking, weak forms and connected speech are reserved for Unit 6.

questions.stem: The sounds /p/ and /b/ can distinguish “pat” and “bat”.
questions.prompt: What is a sound unit that can distinguish meaning called?
questions.explanation: A phoneme is a distinctive sound unit that can distinguish one word from another.

questions.stem: Symbols such as /ʃ/, /θ/ and /ə/ represent speech sounds.
questions.prompt: Which system do these symbols belong to?
questions.explanation: The IPA is a system for representing speech sounds.

questions.stem: Think about the first sound in “ship”.
questions.prompt: Which IPA symbol represents this sound?
questions.explanation: The first sound in “ship” is /ʃ/.

questions.stem: Think about the first sound in “think”.
questions.prompt: Which IPA symbol represents this sound?
questions.explanation: The first sound in “think” is /θ/.

questions.stem: A teacher writes /ˈtiːtʃə/ next to the word “teacher”.
questions.prompt: What does this notation mainly represent?
questions.explanation: Phonemic transcription represents pronunciation using phonemic symbols.

questions.stem: Think about the first sound in “judge”.
questions.prompt: Which IPA symbol represents this sound?
questions.explanation: The first sound in “judge” is /dʒ/.

questions.stem: Think about the final sound in “sing”.
questions.prompt: Which IPA symbol represents this sound?
questions.explanation: The final sound in “sing” is /ŋ/ in standard pronunciation.

questions.stem: Which definition best describes a phoneme?
options: A distinctive sound unit that can contrast meaning
questions.correctAnswer: A distinctive sound unit that can contrast meaning
questions.explanation: A phoneme is a sound category that can distinguish words and meanings.

questions.stem: Think about the first sound in “this”.
questions.prompt: Which IPA symbol represents this sound?
questions.explanation: The first sound in “this” is /ð/.

questions.stem: Why are IPA symbols useful in language teaching?
questions.explanation: IPA symbols represent sounds independently of ordinary spelling.

questions.stem: Which of these is a vowel sound?
questions.explanation: /iː/ is a vowel sound.

questions.stem: Which of these is a consonant sound?
questions.explanation: /m/ is a consonant sound.

questions.stem: In standard British English, consider the vowel in “cat”.
questions.explanation: The vowel in standard British English “cat” is commonly represented by /æ/.

questions.stem: Which sound is a consonant?
questions.explanation: /ŋ/ is a consonant sound, as at the end of “sing”.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes vowel and consonant sounds?
options: Vowels have relatively open airflow; consonants involve some obstruction or narrowing
Vowels occur only in stressed syllables
questions.correctAnswer: Vowels have relatively open airflow; consonants involve some obstruction or narrowing
questions.explanation: Consonants involve a degree of closure or narrowing; vowels generally have more open airflow.

questions.stem: Which symbol represents a vowel sound?
questions.explanation: /ʌ/ is a vowel sound.

questions.stem: Which symbol represents a consonant sound?
questions.explanation: /ʒ/ is a consonant sound.

questions.stem: Which pair contains two vowel phonemes?
questions.explanation: Both /ɪ/ and /iː/ are vowel phonemes.

questions.stem: Which symbol represents the weak central vowel called schwa?
questions.explanation: Schwa is represented by /ə/.

questions.stem: Which statement is true?
options: A vowel sound can form the nucleus of a syllable
Every consonant must be followed by a written vowel
Every vowel letter represents the same sound
questions.correctAnswer: A vowel sound can form the nucleus of a syllable
questions.explanation: A vowel sound normally forms the central part of a syllable.

questions.stem: Say /z/ while touching your throat. You can feel vibration.
questions.explanation: A voiced sound is produced with vocal-fold vibration.

questions.stem: Which sound is unvoiced?
questions.explanation: /s/ is unvoiced; /z/ and /d/ are voiced.

questions.stem: Which pair differs mainly in voicing?
questions.explanation: /f/ is unvoiced and /v/ is voiced.

questions.stem: Which sound is voiced?
questions.explanation: /b/ is voiced; /p/ and /t/ are unvoiced.

questions.stem: A teacher asks learners to touch their throats while contrasting /s/ and /z/.
questions.prompt: Which feature is the teacher highlighting?
questions.explanation: The activity makes vocal-fold vibration noticeable.

questions.stem: Which pair contrasts an unvoiced sound with its voiced counterpart?
questions.explanation: /t/ is unvoiced and /d/ is voiced.

questions.stem: Which sound is voiced?
questions.explanation: /v/ is voiced.

questions.stem: Which pair is distinguished mainly by voicing?
questions.explanation: /ʃ/ is unvoiced and /ʒ/ is voiced.

questions.stem: What happens during the production of a voiced sound?
options: The sound must be a vowel
questions.explanation: Voiced sounds involve vibration of the vocal folds.

questions.stem: Which classroom technique most directly helps learners notice voicing?
options: Feeling throat vibration while producing contrasting sounds
questions.correctAnswer: Feeling throat vibration while producing contrasting sounds
questions.explanation: Touching the throat makes voicing physically noticeable.

questions.stem: “ship” /ʃɪp/ and “sheep” /ʃiːp/ differ by one phoneme.
questions.explanation: A minimal pair contains two words that differ by one phoneme and have different meanings.

questions.stem: Which pair is a minimal pair?
questions.explanation: “Fan” and “van” differ by one phoneme: /f/ and /v/.

questions.stem: Why are minimal pairs useful in pronunciation teaching?
options: They help learners notice sound contrasts that can change meaning
questions.correctAnswer: They help learners notice sound contrasts that can change meaning
questions.explanation: Minimal pairs make meaningful phonemic contrasts clear.

questions.stem: Which pair is NOT a minimal pair?
questions.explanation: These words differ in several sounds and syllables.

questions.stem: A learner confuses “light” and “right”, so the teacher contrasts /l/ and /r/.
questions.explanation: The two words differ by one phoneme.

questions.stem: Which pair is a minimal pair?
questions.explanation: “Thin” and “sin” differ by one phoneme.

questions.stem: “cap” and “cab” differ only in their final consonant phoneme.
questions.explanation: They differ by one phoneme and have different meanings.

questions.stem: Which pair is NOT a minimal pair?
questions.explanation: The words differ in several phonemes and syllables.

questions.stem: A pronunciation exercise contrasts /ɪ/ and /iː/ using “ship” and “sheep”.
options: To help learners discriminate between two phonemes
questions.correctAnswer: To help learners discriminate between two phonemes
questions.explanation: Minimal-pair work develops perception and production of sound contrasts.

questions.stem: Which feature must be true for two words to form a minimal pair?
options: They differ by only one phoneme in the same position
They belong to the same word family
questions.correctAnswer: They differ by only one phoneme in the same position
questions.explanation: A minimal pair differs in one phonemic contrast while the rest of the sound sequence remains the same.

questions.stem: In “TEAcher”, the first syllable is more prominent.
questions.explanation: Word stress is the prominence given to one syllable within a word.

questions.stem: How many syllables are there in “banana”?
questions.explanation: “Banana” has three syllables: ba-na-na.

questions.stem: Which word is typically stressed on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: “Hotel” is typically stressed on the second syllable: ho-TEL.

questions.stem: Compare “PHOtograph” and “phoTOGraphy”.
options: Word stress can shift within a word family
questions.correctAnswer: Word stress can shift within a word family
questions.explanation: Related words can have different stress patterns.

questions.stem: Which statement about word stress is correct?
options: One syllable in a multisyllabic word is typically more prominent than the others
Word stress refers only to volume
questions.correctAnswer: One syllable in a multisyllabic word is typically more prominent than the others
questions.explanation: A stressed syllable is relatively prominent through features such as length, pitch and intensity.

questions.stem: Which word is typically stressed on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: “Banana” is typically ba-NA-na.

questions.stem: Which notation shows first-syllable stress in “teacher”?
questions.explanation: Capitalising the stressed syllable is a common teaching convention.

questions.stem: Which pair best illustrates a stress shift within a word family?
questions.explanation: The main stress shifts across related forms.

questions.stem: What must learners identify to mark word stress accurately?
questions.explanation: Word stress is marked by identifying the syllable with primary prominence.

questions.stem: Why can incorrect word stress reduce intelligibility?
options: Listeners rely partly on expected stress patterns to recognise words
Stress changes every consonant into a vowel
Word stress is part of spelling
questions.correctAnswer: Listeners rely partly on expected stress patterns to recognise words
questions.explanation: Unexpected stress may make a familiar word harder to recognise.

questions.stem: In natural speech, some words in a sentence are more prominent than others.
questions.explanation: Sentence stress is the relative prominence of words or syllables within an utterance.

questions.stem: In “I bought a NEW laptop”, “NEW” is especially prominent.
options: Change the word into a noun
questions.explanation: Sentence stress can highlight important or contrastive information.

questions.stem: Which words are most likely to carry stress in a neutral sentence?
questions.explanation: Content words such as nouns, main verbs, adjectives and adverbs commonly carry sentence stress.

questions.stem: Why might a speaker stress “SHE” in “SHE sent the email”?
options: To contrast her with another possible sender
To show that “she” is a noun
questions.correctAnswer: To contrast her with another possible sender
questions.explanation: Contrastive stress highlights a particular element of meaning.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sentence stress?
options: Prominence can move depending on meaning and focus
The first word is always stressed
Sentence stress is identical to word stress
questions.correctAnswer: Prominence can move depending on meaning and focus
questions.explanation: Sentence stress is flexible and can signal focus and contrast.

questions.stem: In “I wanted the BLUE one”, stressing “BLUE” most likely highlights:
questions.explanation: Contrastive stress can signal correction or contrast.

questions.stem: Which kinds of words most commonly receive sentence stress in neutral speech?
questions.explanation: Content words usually convey the key lexical information.

questions.stem: Compare “I sent the EMAIL” and “I SENT the email.”
options: The focus or contrast of the message
questions.correctAnswer: The focus or contrast of the message
questions.explanation: Moving sentence stress changes which information is especially important.

questions.stem: Which statement about sentence stress is correct?
options: It can vary according to the speaker's intended focus
It always falls on the final word
questions.correctAnswer: It can vary according to the speaker's intended focus
questions.explanation: Sentence stress can shift with emphasis and meaning.

questions.stem: A learner stresses every word equally in a sentence.
questions.prompt: What is the most relevant pronunciation issue?
questions.explanation: Natural speech normally gives some words greater prominence than others.
